title: Read the Crossing Signal
goal: Find when the crossing is safe.
firstImpression: A trolley waits behind a stop bar; the gate lamp has a moving mechanical shutter.
controls: cycle-drum: turn one notch to replay a slow demonstration
clues: The trolley remains stopped during two bell strokes and moves only when the lamp shutter closes.
A two-notch drum and a walking trolley symbol mirror the sounds; darkness alone is not the clue.
steps: Enter the stone recess; the demonstration cannot harm Mara.
Replay the cycle; notch one and notch two rise with the two bells.
Select the walking-trolley symbol after notch two, while the lamp shutter is closed.
The safe phase stays pinned on the drum beside the exit.
wrong: Selecting an earlier phase leaves the stop bar down; replay remains available.
hints: Watch the trolley rather than the distant silhouette.
Count the two raised notches.
Choose the walking symbol after the second notch.
completion: The player identifies the safe phase after seeing or stepping through one complete cycle.
entry: Arrive from new game with Elian’s cassette. This encounter can be examined immediately; commits follow its stated prerequisites.

mapping.note: Does not independently mark the legacy room primary objective complete. Keep source clue IDs crossing-rule. Observe mapped source objects only after the corresponding fact is actually presented; never auto-award all clues on room entry.

pressure: Use the shared room exposure budget, initially the source allocation of 150 seconds, not a fresh full timer per encounter. Advance only during active world manipulation after a safe clue demonstration. At 50% show the room warning with a stable warning icon: “The indicator turns amber. A second bell is gathering in the iron.” At 80% show its critical caption and distinct double-border marker: “A figure stands inside the fog. The shelter is still open.” At the room limit release held controls safely and use the established retreat: You step behind the stone recess. Something crosses where you were standing. It never enters the marked shelter. Never destroy required evidence. Menus, hints, required captions/consequence explanations and user-requested journal reading pause exposure; normal close inspection keeps the world active unless a required explanation is on screen. Source allocations are tuning starting points, not measured encounter durations. Passive warning icons and ambient captions do not pause time; only an explicitly opened required explanation does.
accessibility: Controls shelter, cycle-drum, crossing-marker must each have a focusable name and a visible response. Pointer drag/rotation has discrete click controls and keyboard previous/next/confirm equivalents. Holds offer press-to-latch and press-to-release assistance; release on blur, pause or scene exit cannot commit a destructive action. Caption all significant sounds; preserve symbol or shape distinctions independently of color. Replay demonstrations by user-stepped stages when timing is assisted. Keep clue text at supported large scale with paging inside the inspection area, and retain a stable back/exit action. Reduced motion replaces continuous movement with labelled state changes while preserving clue order.
persistence: Proposed Investigation-owned logical record: encounterId=TG-01, definitionVersion=1, confirmedStep (0 through 4), completed, and a validated control-value record keyed only by shelter, cycle-drum, crossing-marker. Decision records additionally store a preview selection separately from the single Narrative/Campaign commit. This is a proposed schema extension, not an existing installed API. Snapshot logical state plus owning-domain effects at one safe commit boundary. Never save DOM nodes, callbacks, drag pointers, audio handles, frame timestamps or an animation position as authority. On restore, reconstruct controls from confirmed state and replay only noncommitting feedback; never award a reward again. An interrupted unconfirmed drag/hold returns to its last stable detent. A wrong attempt resets only the local unsolved control sequence specified above; verified clues, items, primary completion and committed choices remain. Validate the whole snapshot and definition version before replacing any live owner; an unknown version leaves the current session unchanged. Entry/exit removes input subscriptions, stops local audio and cancels uncommitted operation receipts. Retry preserves original branch commitments and can always return to the named shelter.

catch: lift while the handle is latched

title: Recover the Stranded Parcel
goal: Mark a recognizable return crossing.
firstImpression: A repair parcel rests on a ledge accessible from the secured freight opening.
clues: The parcel carries an existing repair-stall marker, not a new quest item.
A return arrow on the eyelet points back through the secured shutter.
steps: Pull the parcel along its existing tether from the safe ledge.
Unfold the pale repair marker and compare its arrow with the return eyelet.
Tie the marker to that eyelet; the crossing gains a persistent landmark.
wrong: Release of the tether lets the parcel rest on a lower stop, never beyond recovery.
hints: Use the tether from shelter.
The marker belongs at the return eyelet.
Tie it where it can be seen from the reverse direction.
completion: Optional marketSafe outcome recorded; lantern acquisition never depends on the parcel.
entry: Arrive from closed-cafe. Complete MS-01 first. Also complete the second required encounter before departure; this optional encounter never supplies its prerequisites.

Its safety stop catches. Never destroy required evidence. An optional detour may cost active time, but skipping it changes no required gate. Menus, hints, required captions/consequence explanations and user-requested journal reading pause exposure; normal close inspection keeps the world active unless a required explanation is on screen.
